To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a provably optimal algorithm for optimizing control libraries, which can be used to improve performance in a number of robotics tasks, including navigation and manipulation, and (2) our method can be used on-line or batched, and can be used in an anytime fashion to handle real-time requirements.

We present an algorithm for optimizing a sequence of candidates for high dimensional control problems, such as robot navigation, that can be used in an online or batch setting with provable performance.

1) the problem of optimizing control libraries is a special case of a general class of optimization problems, 2) this problem is efficiently solvable using existing algorithms and can be solved in real-time, 3) the resulting control library is provably optimal with respect to the metric of interest.

the optimization of high-dimensional control libraries for robotic systems.
developing a general approach to efficiently optimizing libraries for control problems in robotics.

the optimization of control libraries is an underexplored area of research with many interesting applications.
